title: Is there enough CD47 and HLA-E on the cells in the first hours?
plain: Two signals tell the immune system's natural killer cells and macrophages to leave the new cells alone. If the cells carry too little of either signal in the first hours, those attackers can destroy them before the other protections matter.
detail: In Design A (Arm 1B), an internal EEF1A1 promoter drives CD47 constitutively (238,004 molecules per cell computational prior; Stage-0 gate at least 200,000) and an internal 5xISRE promoter drives HLA-E (release gate at least 15,000 molecules per cell, while the proposed Design X signal aims for 25,000; 10,890 computational resting prior). Endogenous B2M read-through is not credited as productive HLA-E expression, and resting surface density on stage 7 beta cells and endothelial cells is unmeasured (rule GY-009). On soluble HLA-E*01:03, none of the six functional human leader peptides in Lin 2023 reaches a 4.0-fold NKG2C-over-NKG2A affinity gap on its own (kept separate from older HLA-E*01:01 monomer assays such as Valés-Gómez 1999), while VMAPRTLFL acts as a tight activating NKG2C control (Lauterbach 2015), so IIP-0016 adds a 20-construct Stage-0 HLA-E comparator panel gated on paired resting and 24-h IFN-gamma NK subset, UL40 CD8+ T-cell and regulatory T-cell assays. IIP-0022 further routes NKG2A- KIR+ (<= 8%) and IL-12/IL-18 SIRPa-low (<= 10%) escape on upper95 bounds, splits Track-2 HLA-C B'-SCT (KIR2DL across >= 6 KIR-typed donors) from held HLA-G1 (LILRB1, PDB 6AEE engineered C42S/L110I/Q115R crystal; held pending product registration and gated at uniform <= 8% upper95 on sorted LILRB1- NKG2A- KIR+ NK cells), and adds matched B2M-/- TIGIT-low/CD226-high NK testing for prospective PVR (CD155 Ala67Thr rs1058402, PDB 3UDW/6O3O/6ARQ; Diong 2023 PMID 37675979; Matsuo 2022 PMID 35947095; Brown 2025 PMID 41202120 vs Chimienti 2022 PMID 36170817) synaptic sign-inversion.
settle: Count CD47 and HLA-E molecules on the surface of edited cells at hour zero with calibrated flow cytometry (QuantiBRITE beads), and run the 20-construct Stage-0 HLA-E comparator panel across paired resting and 24-h IFN-gamma sorted NKG2A+/NKG2C- and adaptive NKG2C+/NKG2A- NK cells, UL40-reactive CD8+ T cells and regulatory CD8+ T cells.
source: Concise specification sections 4.1 and 9; rule GY-009; IIP-0016 and IIP-0022

title: Does SERPINB9 really block the killer-cell toxin as designed?
plain: Killer immune cells fire a toxin called granzyme B into their targets. The design makes the cells carry SERPINB9, a protein that should block that toxin, and Stage-0 checks compare the reference 2A-linked version with scar-free SERPINB9 templates. A computer cannot tell us whether it works, so only a lab test can.
detail: The flexible reactive-centre loop of SERPINB9 that engages granzyme B (Sun 1996, PMID 8910377; Bird 1998, PMID 9774654; granzyme B reference crystal PDB 1IAU is complexed with Ac-IEPD-CHO rather than SERPINB9, Rotonda 2001, PMID 11325591) cannot be modelled reliably by structure prediction. Canonical CXCL10::SERPINB9-GSG-P2A-PD-L1 also leaves a 21-amino-acid C-terminal P2A tail on SERPINB9, so Stage-0 checks compare it head to head against materialized scar-free (2A-free) dual-promoter SERPINB9 donors (L3-BF-B, 4,078 bp, and DX-L3, 3,799 bp; IIP-0015 and IIP-0017) alongside exploratory redox-substituted SERPINB9 C341S in ARM6 (Mangan 2016, PMID 26670609; IIP-0018).
settle: Compare cells carrying the canonical GSG-P2A SERPINB9 cassette, the scar-free 2A-free dual-promoter SERPINB9 donors and exploratory SERPINB9 C341S against granzyme B and perforin/peroxynitrite stress.
source: Concise specification sections 4.3 and 9; IIP-0015, IIP-0017 and IIP-0018

title: Can the patient's own immune cells restart the attack using debris from the graft?
plain: Cells with no HLA flags are hard for T cells to see directly. But the patient's own immune cells can pick up debris from the graft, show it to T cells, and release inflammatory IL-1 and Fas-ligand signals that attack nearby beta cells.
detail: Donor B2M-/- and CIITA-/- block direct presentation but not indirect presentation of shed secretome and debris by host dendritic cells on HLA-DQ2/DQ8 (rule GY-010). Across a 22-species human-Swiss-Prot-subtracted census (IIP-0017), porcine teschovirus-1 GSG-P2A adds internal and uncleaved-readthrough stretches that were never directly tested in Arber 2013 (PMID 23698740, which assayed T2A, E2A and F2A rather than porcine P2A), while switching to existing 2A-free CXCL10 test donors trims reference-unmatched 8-to-11-mers in Design A from 319 to 235 (mature species) or 391 to 269 (including precursors and readthrough). Screening 112 germline type 1 diabetes genetic regions from the top 200 OpenTargets entries (Robertson 2021, PMID 34127860; Chiou 2021, PMID 34012112) ruled out 16 misleading beta-cell knockout targets—including the 16p13 nearest-gene mitophagy regulator CLEC16A (Soleimanpour 2014, PMID 24949970, vs chromatin-looped DEXI, Dos Santos 2019, PMID 30478640), protective survival brakes PTPN2, TNFAIP3, BACH2 (Marroquí 2014, PMID 24608439), CTSH (Fløyel 2014, PMID 24982147), SOCS1, GLIS3, DLK1 and INS, necroptosis brakes CASP8/FADD (Kaiser 2011, PMID 21368762), and CXCL10 switch blocks JAK1, STAT1, IFNGR1, IRF1 and TNFRSF1A—and converged on IL1R1 and FAS bystander execution receptors. IIP-0018 therefore pre-registers a held 6-arm Locus-3 Multi-miR(IL1R1 + FAS) synthetic-intron Stage-0 challenger suite (4,398-bp donor / 4,688 bp single-AAV6, zero added foreign peptides in primary ARM5; Amen 2022, Fellmann 2013) plus seven standalone zero-bystander FAS/IL1R1 cytosine-base-editor stop comparators while retiring soluble endothelial IL1R2 decoys (Thomas 2012); none is yet measured. IIP-0022 also records off-grid guardrails for constrained TNFRSF1A (gnomAD v4 pLI = 0.9999) and lineage-separated necroptosis (beta-cell resistance to canonical TNF/BV6/zVAD necroptosis in mouse and human EndoC-betaH1 models, Zhao 2015 PMID 25301392; Takiishi 2023 PMID 36707047; Veli 2024 PMID 39004142, vs susceptible vascular endothelium, plus product-specific efferocytosis checks on adhesion-knockout proposals, Hammer 2024 PMID 38981470; Saha 2025 PMID 40796566).
settle: Mix the patient's antigen-presenting and T cells with debris from flag-free islets (comparing canonical P2A, 2A-free CXCL10 test templates, the 6-arm Locus-3 Multi-miR(IL1R1 + FAS) challenger suite and standalone FAS/IL1R1 stop comparators across HLA-DQ2.5/DQ8/DR3/DR4 donors), and look for T-cell activation and bystander cell damage.
source: Concise specification sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, 8 and 9; rule GY-010; IIP-0017, IIP-0018 and IIP-0022

title: Does one kept HLA-C gene calm natural killer cells without displaying a new target?
plain: Design B keeps one matched HLA-C gene so that natural killer cells see the cells as the patient's own. It is not yet known whether a single copy gives enough calming signal, or whether Design B2's optional TYK2 P1104A edit displays a foreign-looking peptide on that kept HLA-C.
detail: After HLA-A and HLA-B deletion, a single retained HLA-C allele must supply enough leader peptide to stabilise surface HLA-E (tracked across IPD-IMGT/HLA SP-1C, SP-2C and SP-3C leader classes in Lin 2023, kept distinct from the HLA-B -21M/-21T leader split in Ramsuran 2018; rule GY-005). In Design B2, installing TYK2 P1104A replaces position-2 proline with an HLA-C-favoured alanine anchor (SPPTKFLEL to SAPTKFLEL; Rasmussen 2014, O'Donnell 2020), while over 90% of recipients carry wild-type TYK2 on both copies; IIP-0017 therefore enforces a fail-closed Stage-0 OR-hold gate across separate G/G, G/C and C/C recipient groups and HLA-C alleles on both islet and vascular cells.
settle: Measure surface HLA-E and natural killer cell response in cells keeping a single HLA-C allele, and test Design B2's TYK2 P1104A SAPTKFLEL peptide by heavy-standard immunopeptidomics and human CD8+ T-cell killing and ELISPOT across separate G/G, G/C and C/C recipient strata on islet and vascular cells.
source: Concise specification sections 4.5 and 9; rule GY-005; IIP-0017

title: Does the oxygen supply hold up under pessimistic assumptions?
plain: A new graft has no blood vessels at first, so it carries its own oxygen for the first three days. In 3D simulations, unpatterned clusters crowd one another, uncoated edge beads create local peroxide spikes, and animal or fungal catalase sheds foreign protein pieces—so Stage-0 tests pair ordered microwells, wet-sieved beads of 50 micrometres or less and strictly recombinant human catalase barrier films at least 20 micrometres thick alongside a 140 micrometre bead-free sheet comparator.
detail: In the 14-day model the homogenized slab average minimum is 19.9 mmHg, while the two-zone cluster model gives a conservative gel-only core oxygen of 2.15 mmHg (0.15 mmHg above the 2.0 mmHg core-necrosis floor; uniform-supply is 4.08 mmHg and homogenized Dirichlet is 8.64 mmHg), alongside an unrounded joint grid of late-connecting and weaker blood vessels and a zero-vessel lower bound (IIP-0002). Twenty of the 21 main PDE regimes also carry over a single unvalidated 68.0-hour oxygen-release half-life from a 25 wt% (10.55 vol%) monolithic silicone disk (Pedraza 2012, PMID 22371586) to 31.25 wt% (13.86 vol%, Layout B) and 46.39 wt% (23.45 vol%, Stage-0 Design X) microbeads with surface-immobilised catalase (IIP-0010). Across an 84-regime fixed-inventory sweep, Stage-0 Design X passes only from 34 to 87 hours at a 36-hour vascular midpoint under first-order or reaction shrinking-core release, narrows to 34 to 68 hours at a 60-hour midpoint, and has no passing half-life when Ginstling-Brounshtein diffusion kinetics combine with a 60-hour midpoint. Resolving discrete clusters and beads in 3D (IIP-0019, IIP-0020) adds local transport and enzyme-species gates: unpatterned pouring at 1,500 IEQ/cm^2 (15 um physical collagen = 45 um hydrogel-equivalent standoff) pushes 40-60% of 100 um clusters below 15 mmHg (vs ordered microwells or dose-matched 80 um clusters at 142.22/152.83 um pitch, distinct from 768 IEQ/cm^2 pitch-held derating); an uncoated edge-touching CaO2 bead creates a 6.9-19.5 uM peroxide plume requiring wet-sieved d_99 <= 50 um beads plus >= 20 um barrier films locked strictly to recombinant human catalase (UniProt P04040, 0 foreign 8-to-11-mers in both 527-aa and Met-cleaved 526-aa forms across 20,429 human Swiss-Prot proteins, disqualifying bovine P00432 and Aspergillus niger P55303 xeno-catalases and enforcing <= 0.10 EU/mg and <= 0.50 EU total-implant endotoxin plus <= 30% 7-day shed-protein mass alongside ~105,429 IU post-cure active load on 333.3 cm^2 to retain 73,800 IU and hold 24-hour burst <= 2.5 uM); and any 140 um bead-free Design Z pouch must pass both 5-site 14-day empty-lumen micro-optode thresholds (Einstein 2023, PMID 38993891) and loaded closed-state confirmation. IIP-0021 further adds a two-scale lineage-partitioned intrinsic-OCR helper to Layer 4 (scaling whole-slab demand as (m_endo + 0.15 * m_vasc) / 1.15 while passing pure-endocrine m_endo to single-cluster BVPs, distinguishing 14.30% vascular cells from 13.04% modeled vascular OCR; Ma 2013 PMID 23935835; Sweet & Gilbert 2006 PMID 17130499; MacDonald 2007 PMID 17503968), shows 25 mmHg plain hydrogel Design Z fails across acute rest, chronic 1.097x demand and 5 vol% PFC (11.4-12.4 mmHg < 15 mmHg), bounds standalone closed-slab Arenicola marina M101 hemoglobin (5 g/L in 10 mL = 2.17 umol vs 5,491 umol CaO2) below 9 seconds above 15 mmHg (Rousselot 2006 PMID 16897713; distinct from air-exposed culture in Lemaire 2023 PMID 37318185), and gates Stage-0 120-hour assembled-organoid respirometry (upper95 <= 0.80, depot t_1/2 >= 72 h) and 4-arm Nec-1s x Ferrostatin-1 pre-conditioning (Aggarwal 2026 PMID 41951603; Takahashi 2012 PMID 23190609; Yuk 2021 PMID 34572979; Bruni 2018 PMID 29789532; Li & Leung 2020 PMID 32893325; washed cell-pellet LC-MS <= LOQ and >= 90% NQO1 activity per Yu 2021 PMID 34252539) while keeping 791.5 mg CaO2 and 36/60-h vascular timing (Van Simaeys 2026 PMID 42547502) unchanged.
settle: Measure crystal and wet-sieved microbead size distributions, oxygen-release half-life, kinetic law, recombinant human P04040 catalase barrier-film peroxide clearance, endotoxin and 7-day activity/shed-mass retention in implanted form; run the 120-hour assembled-organoid OCR coupon and 4-arm Nec-1s x Ferrostatin-1 washed-pellet/NQO1 conditioning check; compare unpatterned vs microwell-spaced 100 um and dose-matched 80 um clusters; and require both empty-lumen micro-optode and loaded closed-state oxygen and hormone confirmation over 14 days.
source: Concise specification sections 5 and 9; IIP-0002, IIP-0010, IIP-0019, IIP-0020 and IIP-0021

title: Do many gene edits at once cause DNA rearrangements?
plain: Each extra edit is another chance for the cell's DNA to be rearranged by mistake, and cells with cancer-linked changes could take over. This is why the scoring model penalises extra edits.
detail: Adenine base editors caused DNA rearrangements in the cited study (PMID 39529170). The project extends that concern to multiple base and prime edits as an engineering precaution (rule GY-006). Open-license CC-BY-4.0 AlphaMissense v3 annotations (Cheng 2023, PMID 37733863) are attached strictly as descriptive context across 27 priority genes and the TYK2 prime-edit window, because 30x whole-genome sequencing misses ~21.5% of 5%-allele-fraction clones and cannot replace >= 63,000x duplex sequencing or manufacturing-scale structural checks (IIP-0017). Inside Stage 0's <= 20% wildcard allocation (IIP-0023), the unscored Design Y landing-pad wildcard compares two-step eePASSIGE 73-bp B2M exon-1 TwinPE excision -> 52-bp attP-in-genome + 11,066-bp 7-unit attB-minicircle (Pandey 2025, PMID 38858586; Levesque 2026, PMID 42749803; avoiding Cas9-DSB AAV capture in Hanlon 2019, PMID 31570731) and 2-locus TadCBEd (Neugebauer 2023, PMID 36357719, gating full C>T + A>G + indel haplotypes) while retaining mandatory CAST-Seq (< 10^-5), k = 0 OT1/OT2/OT4/WGS pseudo-site checks and >= 63,000x TP53/PPM1D/BCOR duplex sequencing. IIP-0024 further enforces paired master-cell-bank and Stage-7 clonal copy-number ([1.85, 2.15]) plus >= 299-cell single-cell mosaicism checks on both 1q32.1 MDM4 (Stavish 2024, PMID 38964325) and 20q11.21 BCL2L1 (Avery 2013, PMID 24286026; Halliwell 2021, PMID 33757297), conjunctive IC1/IC2/IG-DMR methylation (Kagami 2010, PMID 20585555; Court 2014, PMID 24402520), female 46,XX X-inactivation competence (k >= 279 / 300 cells; Mekhoubad 2012, PMID 22560080; Patel 2017, PMID 27989715), >= 1,000x NUMT-filtered mtDNA sequencing (< 5% pathogenic SNV VAF, < 1% deletion burden, Seahorse reserve >= 1.5x; Perales-Clemente 2016, PMID 27436875; Kang 2016, PMID 27151456), and Donor-1 paired lot blocking (n >= 6; Kilpinen 2017, PMID 28489815) with >= 2 unrelated ABO O/O seedlines (6 + 6 exact Welch 90% TOST; rules GY-018 and GY-019).
settle: Deep duplex sequencing (>= 63,000x), long-read phasing, paired bank-and-Stage-7 1q32.1 MDM4 and 20q11.21 copy-number and >= 299-cell mosaicism checks, IC1/IC2/IG-DMR methylation, 46,XX X-inactivation and 1,000x mtDNA screening across >= 2 unrelated O/O donor banks (6 + 6 batches).
source: Concise specification sections 4.5, 4.6, 6 and 9; rules GY-006, GY-018 and GY-019; IIP-0017, IIP-0023 and IIP-0024

title: Which starting assumptions drive the scores?
plain: The scores are estimates, not predictions. Almost all of the difference between designs comes from the team's starting assumptions and very little from published findings. Lab results will replace the assumptions one at a time.
detail: {{assumptions}} per cent of the spread in scores across the {{designs}} designs comes from starting assumptions, {{overlap}} per cent from the overlap of assumptions and findings, and {{findingsShare}} per cent from published findings.
settle: Replace each assumption with a measurement as lab results arrive, starting with the ones that move the scores most.
source: Concise specification sections 7 and 9

title: Which form of CD47 is best: the full-length protein or a surface-anchored form?
plain: CD47 tells macrophages not to eat the cell. The full-length version also sends signals inside the cell that can blunt insulin release. A shorter, surface-anchored version leaves out the inside signals and keeps the macrophage signal. Whether insulin release is spared is not yet tested, so the two are being compared.
detail: Full-length CD47 can blunt glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (Ghimire 2023, PMID 37820008) and block new blood vessels. An IgV-GPI form kept the macrophage signal without cell death or blocked blood-vessel growth in non-islet immune, blood-stem-cell and endothelial models (Jurkat, A20, mouse LSK cells and EA.hy926 endothelial plugs; Xu 2024, PMID 38508139, Tier 2B), while the 180,000 to 220,000 molecules-per-cell protection transition in Hu 2023 (PMID 37156915) comes from virus-titrated primary human islets measured with clone CC2C6 and Quantibrite beads (engineered HIP cells reached over 600,000; IIP-0008). Insulin release and macrophage protection with IgV-GPI in stem-cell islets remain untested.
settle: Compare insulin release and macrophage protection side by side for each CD47 form in stem-cell islets, cross-calibrating clone B6H12 and clone CC2C6 Quantibrite surface counts.
source: Concise specification section 4.1; IIP-0008

title: Which layout should be used to add CD47 and HLA-E at B2M?
plain: Two layouts for adding CD47 and HLA-E at B2M are being compared, alongside a 20-variant HLA-E panel to avoid triggering activating NKG2C natural killer cells while fitting inside one delivery virus.
detail: Layout 1 (Arm 1A) joins the genes with a porcine GSG-P2A sequence (4,880 base pairs, over the single-AAV6 limit and carrying uncleaved 697-aa readthrough risk; IIP-0017). Layout 2 (Arm 1B, 3,974 base pairs, alongside 4,143-bp Embodiment A*) uses separate promoters facing opposite directions with no 2A joint and fits in one AAV6 virus, paired in Stage 0 with silent B2M exon-2 stop-seam hardening against a 32-aa out-of-frame tail (IIP-0015) and a 20-construct two-strand splice-cleaned HLA-E NKG2C/NKG2A comparator panel (Lin 2023, PMID 37264229; Lauterbach 2015, PMID 26382247; IIP-0016).
settle: Compare Layout 1, Layout 2 and the 20-construct splice-cleaned HLA-E comparator panel across resting and interferon-stimulated islet and vascular cells for surface density, splicing fidelity, promoter methylation, editing yield and NK/CD8 response.
source: Concise specification section 4.1; rule GY-009; IIP-0015, IIP-0016 and IIP-0017

title: At CXCL10, does it matter which protective gene comes first?
plain: The design adds SERPINB9 and PD-L1 at CXCL10 so they switch on only during inflammation. Stage-0 tests compare the SERPINB9-first reference cassette against the reverse order, scar-free 2A-free donors, and a 6-arm synthetic-intron IL-1 and Fas receptor shield inside one AAV6 virus.
detail: Locus 3 is CXCL10::SERPINB9-GSG-P2A-PD-L1, compared head-to-head with CXCL10::PD-L1-GSG-P2A-SERPINB9, scar-free (2A-free) dual-promoter L3-BF-B (4,078 bp) and DX-L3 (3,799 bp) donors with antisense-ART3 splice hardening (IIP-0015, IIP-0017), and a held 6-arm 5'-UTR synthetic-intron Multi-miR(IL1R1 + FAS) Stage-0 challenger suite built on the 2A-free L3-BF-B backbone (4,398-bp donor / 4,688 bp single-AAV6; IIP-0018) gated on calibrated UMI splicing, >= 85% retained SERPINB9/PD-L1 induction, >= 90% miR-375 AGO2 occupancy (Poy 2004), unblunted postprandial IL-1beta-amplified GSIS (Dror 2017) and >= 99.99% AP1903 iCasp9 kill.
settle: Edit cells with each order and with the 6-arm Multi-miR(IL1R1 + FAS) synthetic-intron challenger panel, comparing SERPINB9/PD-L1 levels, splicing fidelity, miR-375 loading, insulin secretion and survival under inflammation and killer-cell attack.
source: Concise specification section 4.3; IIP-0015, IIP-0017 and IIP-0018

title: Does a sequence in Design B's CXCL10 edit act as an unintended switch?
plain: Design B drops one linking sequence at the CXCL10 spot to avoid leaving a piece that the kept HLA-C gene could show to T cells as foreign. In exchange, a piece of the design might switch genes on at the wrong time. That has to be ruled out.
detail: Design B uses a 2A-free layout at the CXCL10 locus, which trims reference-unmatched 8-to-11-mers from 205 to 83 in wild-type-TYK2 Design B and from 243 to 121 in Design B2 (IIP-0017). However, an internal promoter or eIF4G leader sequence can have cryptic promoter activity (PMID 12370285).
settle: Test whether the sequence drives expression on its own, outside inflammation.
source: Concise specification sections 4.5 and 9; IIP-0017

title: Can the safety switch remove almost every cell?
plain: Every cell carries a safety switch that a drug (AP1903) should trigger to remove them. The proposed target is fewer than one cell in 100 million able to regrow. Nothing has shown that yet.
detail: iCasp9 is inserted on both AAVS1 copies from a promoter active in every cell type, flanked by an HNRNPA2B1-proximal 455 bp CpG-core anti-silencing candidate (GRCh38 chr7:26200580-26201034; CBX3 is a legacy alias, not proof of identity to the published CBX3-side fragment). Stage-0 tests compare four anti-silencing and orientation arms alongside matched 2x2 co-directional and convergent splice-cleaned comparators (Knight 2012, PMID 22696657; excluding intron-blocking SPA poly(A) inside PPP1R12C) while checking host-gene (PPP1R12C) splicing, calibrated minigene and clonal UMI junction sequencing (at least 3,700 UMIs), double-stranded RNA stress and DNA methylation alongside the untouched reference donor, and audit local geometry across three crystal structures of the switch's domains (PDB 1BL4, 1JXQ and 1NW9, reconciling 565/746 canonical vs 562/746 insertion-code-inclusive heavy-atom pairs < 2.2 A on 1NW9/1JXQ; IIP-0011, IIP-0015 and IIP-0024). The bound of one in 100 million counts only cells able to regrow, which is a different endpoint from the early bulk-kill screen (99.9% of cells killed), and IIP-0024 enforces strict pre-normalisation integer (k, n) cell counts, exact independent recovery-calibrated bounds U95 = (1 - 0.05**(1/n)) / eta (rejecting floor(n * eta) or unverified cluster-design shortcuts), sister-unit Day-90 Gate 0S en-bloc recovery (L95_t >= 0.99) plus dual < 10^-6 shedding (n >= 2,995,731), and monotonic safety-stop latching across batches (Di Stasi 2011, PMID 22047558; Wunderlich 2022, PMID 35795779; rule GY-018). Killing efficiency in hypoxic, immature or rogue cells across all 9.335 x 10^8 total living cells (including endothelial and pericyte support cells) is unmeasured (rule GY-002 excludes lineage-restricted switches). For the unscored Stage-0 Design Y landing-pad wildcard (IIP-0023), where cHS4 + HNRNPA2B1 UCOE + UBC-iCasp9 sits as the 7th transcription unit inside a biallelic 11,066-bp B2M minicircle, gate Y-04 additionally checks 60-day multi-cistron co-retention against supercoiling coupling (Naughton 2013, PMID 23416946; Gilbert 2014, PMID 24584092) and requires k = 0 clonogenic survivors across N_eff = N * f_clonogenic * eta >= 299,573,228 effective trials (exact Poisson upper95 <= 1.0e-8).
settle: Compare the AAVS1 anti-silencing, orientation and splice-cleaned arms across maturation with calibrated minigene and UMI junction sequencing, check PPP1R12C splicing, double-stranded RNA stress and CpG methylation, and give AP1903 to edited cultures, including at low oxygen, to count integer clonogenic survivors against exact recovery-calibrated bounds.
source: Concise specification sections 4.4, 4.6 and 9; IIP-0011, IIP-0015, IIP-0023 and IIP-0024

title: Is switching off TYK2 worth its cost in insulin-making cells, or does TYK2 P1104A avoid it?
plain: In Design B1, switching off TYK2 helps against inflammatory signalling in the model, but costs about a third of the insulin-making cells while they grow. Design B2 instead tests the naturally protective TYK2 P1104A variant to spare cell yield, provided it does not create a foreign peptide on kept HLA-C.
detail: Design B1 disrupts TYK2, where Chandra 2022 (PMID 36289205) reports about 32 per cent fewer insulin-making cells during stem-cell islet differentiation. Design B2 (evaluated in the four-hurdle assessment) instead preserves wild-type TYK2 or installs the catalytic-domain protective variant TYK2 P1104A (rs34536443; Dendrou 2016, PMID 27807284; Boisson-Dupuis 2018, PMID 30578352) to dampen type-I interferon signalling while retaining TYK2 scaffolding, gated on IIP-0017's stratified HLA-C SAPTKFLEL presentation and CD8+ T-cell hold checks (OQ-004).
settle: Compare wild-type TYK2, TYK2 knockout (B1) and TYK2 P1104A (B2) head to head in the Design B chassis for Stage-7 beta-cell yield, interferon protection and HLA-C SAPTKFLEL antigenicity.
source: Concise specification section 4.5; OQ-004; IIP-0011 and IIP-0017

title: X is two different candidates, not one verified product
plain: The name Design X covers two separate things: a scored comparison on the 2,160-design grid (Design A plus one insulin-gene base edit, using the baseline 119 micrometre oxygen layer) and an unscored Stage-0 upgrade suite (new B2M switch, 20-variant HLA-E selectivity panel and CD47 variant, an intronic IL-1 and Fas receptor knockdown or base-editor stop comparators, a protective insulin-gene cell line, an outer-ring Fas-ligand gel tested alongside a streptavidin-free human cuff comparator, and an ordered-microwell, human-catalase-buffered 100 micrometre oxygen layer, with no insulin-gene edit). Neither is built or tested.
detail: Clarified in IIP-0009 and expanded with Stage-0 comparators in IIP-0016, IIP-0018, IIP-0019 and IIP-0020. The scored grid candidate (ISLET1_CHASSIS_X_EMERGENT_CHALLENGER, K=4, B=1) adds an INS base edit to Design A on the baseline 119 micrometre Layout B oxygen layer and is tied for second place on the grid. The separate Stage-0 molecular and pouch suite (K=4, B=0) tests a new B2M promoter, CD47 sequence and 20-construct S10 HLA-E NKG2C/NKG2A selectivity panel (IIP-0016), a 6-arm CXCL10 synthetic-intron Multi-miR(IL1R1 + FAS) donor alongside standalone zero-bystander FAS/IL1R1 CBE stop comparators (IIP-0018), an INS-VNTR Class III starting line, an outer-ring SA-FasL gel layout challenged in anti-PEG and Day-28 anti-streptavidin human sera alongside a streptavidin-free CFH[19-448] + THBD[363-497]-Cys + ADIPOQ-Hexa-FasL comparator on self-hydrolyzing DPR-maleimide linkers (IIP-0020), and ordered microwells with <= 50 micrometre CaO2 beads and a >= 20 micrometre recombinant human P04040 catalase barrier film around a 100 micrometre central oxygen layer (IIP-0019, IIP-0020), behind pre-registered lab pass gates.
settle: Keep separate identities, provide the exact donor and protein ledger, and qualify each product before any promotion.
source: Concise specification sections 3 and 4.6; IIP-0009, IIP-0016, IIP-0018, IIP-0019 and IIP-0020

title: Does the proposed outer-band pouch physically fit?
plain: In the baseline geometry used for the scores across Designs A, B and X, a 350 micrometre slab with a 119 micrometre central oxygen layer leaves two outer bands of 115.5 micrometres, slightly narrower than 120 micrometre cell clusters. Explicit 3D checks also showed that loose clusters clump together and that uncoated edge beads spike local peroxide, so the Stage-0 layouts add ordered microwells, wet-sieved beads of at most 50 micrometres and catalase barrier films at least 20 micrometres thick (at 350 or expanded 390 micrometres) alongside a 140 micrometre bead-free pre-vascularised comparator. Nothing has been built or measured yet.
detail: Clarified in IIP-0009 and audited in 3D in IIP-0019. In the scored Layout B baseline shared by the grid rows for Designs A, B and X, a 350 micrometre slab with a 34% central lamina (119 micrometres) leaves two 115.5 micrometre outer bands, too narrow to contain 120 micrometre spheres without compression. Stage-0 Embodiment A* and Stage-0 Design X thin the central lamina to 100 micrometres (clusters <= 80 to 100 micrometres) and pair ordered microwells with wet-sieved d_99 <= 50 micrometre beads and >= 20 micrometre cell-free catalase-immobilised barrier films across expanded 390 micrometre or 350 micrometre cross-sections while holding 791.5 mg CaO2 conserved, alongside a two-stage 140 micrometre Zero-CaO2 bead-free pre-vascularised comparator (IIP-0019). All layouts remain unbuilt.
settle: Reconcile local cell packing, microwell spacing, sieved bead inventory, catalase barrier retention and cluster dimensions in physical prototypes before claiming an oxygen improvement.
source: Concise specification section 5; IIP-0009 and IIP-0019

title: Which assumptions and definition of success sit behind the four-hurdle odds estimate?
plain: The 27%, 31% and 36% single-design figures (Designs A, B and X) and the 53% three-design figure are uncalibrated computational judgements for clearing four in-body hurdles in sequence, assuming the edited cells work as designed and pass lab safety checks before any trial. Layering new untested edits or biomaterial shields together can shift earlier human-anchored hurdles too, moving from one design to three depends on how much the designs overlap at each hurdle, and the estimate depends on which clinical outcome counts as success.
detail: Raised in IIP-0003 (issue #3) and reassessed on 2026-11-16 after IIP-0016..IIP-0020. Each step in the four-hurdle estimate is judged for a design still in the running after the earlier hurdles, with three-design conditional pass rates (88% x 87% x 86% x 80%) derived from an explicit 4,096-state (2^12) common-shock tree across Designs A (27.0%, ~27%), B (31.1%, ~31%) and X (36.3%, ~36%) giving 52.59% (about 53%; 52.22% if Hurdle-3 common shock stays fixed at c_3 = 0.88) for three locked products or 55.63% under Stage-0 cell-line by pouch modularity (up from 21% and 37% on 2026-11-05, and 26% / 31% / 34% / 51.48% on 2026-11-15). Lab release gates (OQ-012 safety-switch escape, OQ-006 DNA rearrangements, and product-specific Gate 1 insulin and glucagon function plus Stage-0 construct and biomaterial gates) sit outside the four hurdles as pre-trial pass/fail conditions, and a single clinical endpoint (such as one-year insulin independence without anti-rejection drugs and without severe hypoglycaemia) must be fixed before replacing starting judgements with data. IIP-0022 replaces hard-coded 2^12 portfolio decimals in Layer 1 with an executable 4,096-state (1,024 positive-mass states) common-shock generator reporting both legacy 3-slot (55.63% modular / 52.59% locked) and shared-A/X 2-route CaO2+catalase pouch unions (54.12% modular / 50.78% locked; 53.16% and 49.71% on the 2026-11-15 DEC-098 baseline), and IIP-0024 enforces strict non-finite and marginal-above-common-shock validation plus logs the conditional two-seedline Hurdle-1 sensitivity (phi_donor = 0.25: 50.78% -> 51.53%-51.74% shared A/X; 52.59% -> 53.33%-53.50% three-slot) while keeping published 27% / 31% / 36% / 53% headline percentages unchanged.
settle: Fix one clinical definition of success, test the per-design and shared failure assumptions in Stage 0-2 experiments, and replace the computational judgements with measured pass rates as lab and preclinical results arrive.
source: IIP-0003, IIP-0016..IIP-0020, IIP-0022, IIP-0024, and the full blueprint (warning 4)

title: Can a Stage-1 multi-lineage immune–islet co-culture catch cross-talk missed by split assays without hiding which edit failed?
plain: Stage 0 tests T cells, natural killer cell subsets and macrophages in separate wells so each gene edit gets a clear pass or fail. In the body those immune cells act together and amplify one another's signals. A combined human immune–islet test in Stage 1 might catch failure modes that split tests miss, provided background donor mismatch and gel recovery do not blur the readout.
detail: Raised in IIP-0007 (issue #7). Stage-0 Readouts 3A, 3B and 3C stay separate and mandatory for clean per-edit attribution. Before adding a supplementary combined human PBMC, antigen-presenting-cell, natural-killer and macrophage co-culture with microgel-embedded stem-cell islets in Stage 1, three technical checks have to pass: separating non-specific donor mismatch from autoimmune attack over 48 to 72 hours, keeping every immune cell type alive in islet medium without artificial cytokine-activated killer effects, and recovering intact clusters from the gel to measure glucose-triggered insulin and glucagon release afterwards (comparing modular human immune co-cultures in Higbee 2009 PMID 19807200, Byers 2009 PMID 19272794 and Ma 2010 PMID 20331478 with autologous stem-cell-islet immune co-culture in Leite 2020 PMID 32668238).
settle: Keep Stage-0 Readouts 3A, 3B and 3C separate, then run a Stage-1 qualification pilot testing 48 to 72 hour background lysis, multi-lineage survival without artificial cytokine activation, and post-challenge insulin secretion recovery.
source: IIP-0007; Stage-0 execution playbook Readout 3

title: Do insulin and glucagon release recover after low oxygen, and can higher-beta mixes match the 60:30:10 default?
plain: Surviving the first 14 days of low oxygen does not guarantee that the cells still release insulin and glucagon properly afterwards. Separately, packing more beta cells into each cluster could shrink the graft if insulin shut-off and low-sugar glucagon rescue still hold up.
detail: Raised in IIP-0004 and IIP-0006. Surviving a 336-hour hypoxic bridge does not establish preserved glucose-regulated insulin secretion, rapid shut-off, or low-glucose glucagon rescue during and after reoxygenation (Wang 2025, PMID 40404627; Chendke 2023, PMID 37476069). Stage 0 measures hormone function after recovery before crediting functional dose, and compares intermediate beta:alpha:delta mixtures (70:20:10, 70:25:5, 80:15:5 and 80:10:10) beside the 60:30:10 default and pure beta-cell controls (Perez-Frances 2024, PMID 39169271), keeping 60:30:10 unless independent batches pass both shut-off and glucagon-rescue checks. IIP-0021 also records conditional 13-state portal exercise insulin-washout lag bounds across 150,000 (v = 0.18, kept distinct from Stage-5A's 25,000-35,000 IEQ forearm sentinel; 4.64 mM preserved paracrine vs 3.53 mM scaled), 300,000 (v = 0.36, T_ins <= 3.64 min) and non-waivable full-dose 500,000 total IEQ (v = 0.60, T_ins <= 1.96-2.71 min), and requires post-washout dynamic GSIS SI >= 3.0, >= 85% absolute insulin output retention and >= 2.0-fold low-glucose alpha-cell glucagon induction after any metabolic-rest or Nec-1s x Ferrostatin-1 conditioning exposure (MacDonald 2007, PMID 17503968).
settle: Measure dynamic insulin secretion, 3-minute shut-off and low-sugar glucagon release after recovery from the 14-day low-oxygen window, and compare intermediate beta:alpha:delta mixtures against 60:30:10 across independent differentiation batches.
source: Concise specification sections 5 and 9; IIP-0004, IIP-0006 and IIP-0021

title: Do the core gene insertions leave nearby genes and splicing intact, and does shed PD-L1 act in the liquid around the graft?
plain: Inserting protective genes at B2M, CXCL10 and AAVS1 or switching off CIITA could accidentally disturb nearby genes, splice in either direction into surrounding host exons, form repeated hairpins in AAV6 templates, or lose promoter activity over time. At CXCL10, enzymes can also clip PD-L1 off the cell surface into the surrounding liquid, where its effect on immune cells is unknown.
detail: Raised in IIP-0005, IIP-0011, IIP-0015 and IIP-0016. Sequence, two-strand splice-motif and repeat scans flag places to test (and reconcile the 326 Class-I and 112 Class-II boundary peptide windows across the reference junctions) without certifying splicing safety, while all canonical reference FASTAs remain untouched. Stage 0 tracks Arm 1B promoter CpG methylation, ships a 20-construct two-strand splice-hardened HLA-E comparator panel at B2M (0 created splice donors or new acceptor coordinates, alongside the silent stop-seam check against splicing into B2M exon 2's 32-amino-acid foreign tail), checks CIITA transcript clean-up, verifies at CXCL10 (4q21.1) that CXCL9, CXCL11 and opposite-strand ART3 stay undisturbed while comparing one-factor-at-a-time synonymous PD-L1 variants (Forrest 2020, PMID 32053646), a bGH 3'-end cleavage check and an optional single-sided 80 bp cHS4 FII element avoiding AAV6 hairpin repeats (Xie 2017, PMID 28462820), runs calibrated EndoC-betaH1 minigene, 5'/3'-RACE and clonal UMI junction sequencing (at least 3,700 UMIs) across Loci 1, 3 and 4, and tests minimally processed cell-free medium conditioned by inflamed edited islets on an independent PD-1 reporter beside protease-shedding assays (Hira-Miyazawa 2018, PMID 29345283). Separately, inside the <= 20% wildcard firewall (IIP-0023), Stage 0 audits the 3-construct Design Y landing-pad FASTA (5'/3'-RACE verifying 0 sense ATGs across the 75-bp B2M 5'-UTR + attR leader, 201-bp vs 601-bp CIITA-pIV CpG-island reconciliation alongside Nunez 2021 PMID 33838111 CRISPRoff and full-length CIITA isoforms PMID 9184229, and hCDH5 + 4x miR-375-3p CD200 iEC:SC-beta >= 50:1 selectivity sparing beta-cell miR-375 and human ADORA1/ADORA2A GSIS, PMID 42660457, PMID 35297680).
settle: Run calibrated host-context minigene assays, 5'/3'-RACE, clonal UMI splice-junction sequencing (at least 3,700 UMIs), host-mRNA equivalence checks and bisulfite methylation assays across resting and inflamed edited islets alongside the one-factor-at-a-time Stage-0 comparators, and test cell-free conditioned medium with and without PD-L1 blockade on a stimulated PD-1 reporter.
source: Concise specification sections 4.1 to 4.6, 6 and 9; IIP-0005, IIP-0011, IIP-0015, IIP-0016 and IIP-0023

title: Do edited islets stay protected after temporary gel signals wear off, and do biomaterial antibodies or shed FasL compromise the cuff?
plain: Temporary gel particles carrying clotting-control and Fas-ligand proteins wash out after the early transplant window, while pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies or Day-28 anti-streptavidin antibodies could neutralise or opsonise the cuff. Stage-0 tests therefore challenge the streptavidin cuff alongside a held all-human CFH, THBD and Hexa-FasL comparator on self-hydrolyzing linkers, and test ectopic CD55 while keeping intracellular CD59 intact.
detail: Raised in IIP-0012 and expanded in IIP-0020. Prior SA-FasL microgel studies used short-course rapamycin in single-dose grafts (where Lei 2022, PMID 35559682 still observed anti-SA-FasL IgG seroconversion alongside tolerability of ~200 ug tethered SA-FasL) and measured fluorescent retention rather than functional depletion half-life (Headen 2018, PMID 29867165; Turan 2024, PMID 38709159). Core bacterial streptavidin is 100% foreign to the human proteome (508/508 8-to-11-mers; baseline human anti-SA reactivity in Berth 2018 PMID 29466233 and Verougstraete 2020 PMID 31782946, plus clinical secondary antibody surges in Breitz 2000 PMID 10647616 and Orozco 2025 PMID 40605797), ~72% of adults carry detectable anti-PEG antibodies (~7% IgG > 500 ng/mL, Yang 2016 PMID 27804292), and unhydrolyzed maleimides can shed soluble oligomeric FasL via retro-Michael exchange (Lyon 2014 PMID 25194818; soluble APO010 hepatotoxicity context in Verbrugge 2009 PMID 19276268, Eisele 2011 PMID 21183510 and Jandu 2020 PMID 32619459). Stage 0 therefore challenges SA-FasL/SA-THBD alongside a held Mode-B human cuff comparator panel (CFH[19-448] + THBD[363-497]-Cys + H1a ADIPOQ-Hexa-FasL on >= 98% ring-hydrolyzed DPR-maleimide linkers, <= 5% 14-day bioactive FasL shedding, and 72-h primary human hepatocyte caspase-3/7 & ALT/LDH <= 1.2x) across >= 12 unpooled human sera stratified by anti-PEG and Day-28 anti-SA IgG (surface C3b and fluid sC5b-9 <= 5%, two-sided FasL EC50 within [0.50, 2.00]x and Emax >= 80%), compares never-conditioned, gel-depleted and active-gel aliquots for immune rebound, tests ectopic CD55(SCR1-4) while preserving endogenous CD59 (Golec 2022 PMID 35666870; van der Torren 2017 PMID 27787618), and holds TYMS, NLRC5, endogenous CD274 and TXNIP outside core designs.
settle: Challenge SA-FasL/SA-THBD and the held DPR-hydrolyzed human CFH + THBD + ADIPOQ-Hexa-FasL cuff comparator across >= 12 unpooled human sera stratified by baseline anti-PEG and Day-28 anti-SA IgG (checking surface C3b, fluid sC5b-9, two-sided FasL EC50/Emax, THBD/CFH retention, <= 5% 14-day bioactive FasL shedding and 72-h primary human hepatocyte safety), compare gel-depleted vs never-treated islets for immune rebound, and test ectopic CD55 alongside intact endogenous CD59.
source: Concise specification sections 4.6, 5 and 9; IIP-0012 and IIP-0020
